This one-time read uses only an already connected phone-control permission channel. It briefly reads at most 1,000 existing fixed-tag keyboard log lines within a 128 KiB budget; these lines may contain private data or be older than 2 minutes. Only known structured events emitted by this App process from the last 2 minutes, timestamps, user-action flags when available, and fixed reasons are retained. Other processes are excluded even if a log line names this App. No typed text, candidates, raw logs or app list is exported. No screen is started, input injected or permission granted. Backgrounding this App or leaving Diagnostics cancels the request and discards in-flight results without closing the shared channel. In multi-window mode, switching focus while Diagnostics remains visible does not revoke an already approved one-time read; results stay in memory until you explicitly publish or export. Once started, the log subprocess runs for at most 1.5 seconds; waiting for a shared channel is not included. Some Android versions (including Android 12) do not log these events: zero events does not mean the keyboard is healthy.

Works only when you ask DSH to do something on your phone: it reads the text on the current screen (and takes a screenshot when needed), then taps, types and swipes as you ask. dsh-go plugin view v1 and v2

A native view a DSH plugin hands to the dsh-go phone app: a tree of components from a fixed catalog (the dsh-ui superset), values optionally bound to the view's data model with {"$": "data.path"}. Used by tool cards (meta["dsh-go/view"]), panels and the composer strip. Strict JSON. Limits JSON Schema cannot express (bytes, node count, depth, children per budget) are listed under x-dsh-go and enforced by the app, which truncates instead of rejecting except for bytes and nesting. Anything the app draws without an issue passes this schema (empty arrays are a legal 'no data yet', long labels are clipped), with three deliberate exceptions where the schema is the stricter author spec: unknown properties (the app ignores them), malformed binding paths (the app shows an em dash) and the alias spellings the app also accepts (success, warning, column, completed, a keyValue 'name'…). Spec: docs/design/native-plugins-views.md.
